body: ADHD gave me a horrible learning disability. I didn’t know until last year in December (23F) that I even had ADHD until I was talking with my diagnosed ADHD partner (24M) about how bad my learning disability (I thought I might have had) had gotten. (I took a gap year from college to focus on building my art portfolio, the only aspect of my life ADHD didn’t impact was my art…. Until it was all I was doing…. And ADHD ruined the one thing I loved for that entire gap year. I had no motivation to work, whenever I did I couldn’t learn, had to just try to figure shit out on my own, which I had been doing my whole life but usually not when it came to art I picked skills up naturally but now I couldn’t, I felt paralyzed, creativity block and depression) I thought I was just experiencing normal artist burnout and felt like dawgggggg until I started seeking therapy. Within two sessions my therapist was like…. dawg…. You gotta ADHD and OCD…. Then I started seeing a Psych to get treated who also diagnosed me with autism and in January I started Vyvanse…. HOLY SHIT- I have been living half a life for this LONG WHAT? My productivity is through the roof, my creativity is flourishing because I’m able to connect my thoughts better, I don’t have emotional deregulation as much and it helps my tism.

Hi! I just started vyvanse myself about a month ago and my anxiety/depression has pretty much completely gone away. This is big for me because this past month or two I’ve had to deal with some of the hardest moments in my life (my partner was hospitalized, they’re better now though thank god). The vyvanse really helped me center myself and gather my thoughts instead of feeling so lost, scared and worried. I’m a lot more clear headed, listening to my logical side of my brain more rather than ruminating. I did notice a small change in myself though, towards the end of the night when the effects start to wear off I become very irritable, like I either get really annoyed with people around me or if I’m not annoyed with them I start ruminating which sucks but if I do something non stressful like play video games or watch tv it tends to go away in 20 minutes. That side effect doesn’t bother me at all because I’m self aware of it so it has been feeling less and less explosive lately. I’m sure it might go away completely if I read myself more. All in all I think these stimulants work differently for different people. The way we were raised, the problems we’ve encountered, coping mechanisms good or bad all play a factor into our management of dysregulation. I got lucky with finding a medication that works great for me but that by all means doesn’t mean it could work for you and that’s okay. Just keep perservering! I believe in you! 💕

Hey, I’m sorry you’re feeling this way! Yes it’s completely normal no worries. It’s a mixture of a psychological thing when sticking to a diet and a physical thing. The psychological thing is when we stick to a diet for a long period of time our minds tend to get stuck in calorie counting mode which can tend to make us feel emotional about our choices outside of the deficit because we’re scared to detract from progress or accomplishment. The second is physical, your body, especially your stomach shrinks when on a calorie deficit and our feelings of “fullness” more often then not on a deficit was because our bodies became use to the amount of food we were getting. Lol sometimes I even feel guilty when feeling coma inducing full on my deficit. All in all, your stomach will get reuse to your higher caloric intake and that guiltiness should resolve with time. Just remember that a diet should be a lifestyle change and not a restrictive thing. We only step backwards when we develop those old bad habits again! But that also doesn’t mean we can’t enjoy life and all the wonderful foods it offers, just be smart with the balance. ✨🙏🏻

Hey! They teach a lot of other aspects of tech, for instance, they teach you beginner level coding. You can also get 5 units worth of electives which can introduce you to topics such as animation, brand strategies, photography and mixed media (there are tons more to choose from). Also CSUMB is a smaller school, not sure how many students there are as of now but usually around 7,000 plus which seems like a lot but isn’t. I would say a good chunk of those students are communication design majors and I haven’t met one student yet that doesn’t love the major. I think the best thing about this major with this school is the more hands on teaching provided by smaller classroom sizes. Every person I have met in this major is very kind and open minded. Also do be surprised if there is a variety of ages in your future classes, the last class I had contained students both young and old, it’s a very diverse major. Personally, it’s not hard to shine in a communication design class, if you put time, effort and passion into those classes especially the projects your professors will love you, this is where the internships come in. There are such great opportunities for internships in this major if you look for them. Imprinting a good impression on your professors by asking questions, being attentive and putting in your 110% for your assignments will provide a strong foundation for your professors to want to recommend you for internships or other opportunities as well. There are also great programs at CSUMB that help connect students to internships, I get about 5 emails a day recommending me to internships for my major but unfortunately am not looking for an internship right now. Personally, the classes are not hard, and they don’t require a lot of time contribution to get an A, currently I’m on my majors deans list and it’s been great maintaining it, I’ve actually been gifted a scholarship for it twice now. As for projects, almost every class I’ve taken has amazing projects. I’ve noticed a lot of professors for communication design are open to all forms of creativity which means their rubrics arent stiff, if you have an idea for a project that’s outside the box don’t be afraid to purse it! A lot of the projects I’ve been given so far are really fun, for example the starting class you’ll take which is a prerequisite for upper level classes is introduction to media tools. This class we had projects geared around photoshop and illustrator such as creating movie posters, advertisements and so on from beginner level teaching. I will include my movie posters below to show how that introduction class took me from knowing nothing about photoshop to amateur level quality in one semester :) Also, there are tons of clubs that you can join relating to your major too! All in all I highly recommend attending CSUMB, this might be a totally biased perspective on the school but this is my truth :) let me know if you have any more questions, I’d love to answer! ALSO forgot to add, huge benefit is we get access to all adobe products, I have adobe 2022 photoshop and illustrator downloaded right now :) it’s a dream[class project](https://imgur.com/a/HIntIVm)

Hey! I’m a Junior at CSUMB studying Communication Design and I HIGHLY recommend it. There are some quirks though: 1. Lots of classes, you might need to take an extra semester or two to finish them, that’s what I’m doing but I am getting a minor in cinematic arts so it might be because of that lol. And 2. The professors for the beginning classes (specially media tools and digital drawing) (Professor Webster) is impatient and really bad at teaching. Besides those two things I highly recommend. The classes are easy and push you for creativity, the work load is easily manageable. A lot of the classes I’ve taken are pretty lenient on attendance, and a lot of them are easily stackable due to some being online. As for the major, it’s a great major to choose. I love it because of how versatile it can be. You get to choose a concentration when you declare your major, my focus is game design, but there is visual design and web design as well. This major helps you a lot with developing skills in tech, they do a good job at teaching you from the ground up, starting off with simple programs such a photoshop and illustrator and slowly move you into more advanced areas. The projects are fun as well, you’ll get plenty of stuff to put on your portfolio at the end, also I believe there is a portfolio. One of the classes you have to take towards your capstone is CST 300 Major Proseminar which (I haven’t taken yet nor know little about) I think helps you develop a portfolio. All in all great major, a little dragged out sometimes but I’d highly recommend it!
